Filter GTFS object by period

Source: R/filter_by_period.R
filter_by_period.Rd

Filters a GTFS object by the services that run on at least one day of a period, keeping (or dropping) the relevant entries in each file.

Usage

filter_by_period(gtfs, start_date, end_date, keep = TRUE, trim = TRUE)

Arguments

gtfs

A GTFS object, as created by read_gtfs().

start_date, end_date

A Date (including IDate) or a string in the "YYYYMMDD" or "YYYY-MM-DD" formats. The first and last days of the period, both included. end_date must not be earlier than start_date.

keep

A logical. Whether the entries related to the services that run in the specified period should be kept or dropped (defaults to TRUE, which keeps the entries).

trim

A logical. Whether the calendars of the kept services should be cut to the period (defaults to TRUE), so that the GTFS object has no service outside it. Ignored when keep is FALSE.

Value

The GTFS object passed to the gtfs parameter, after the filtering process.

Details

The services are selected as when filtering by each day of the period with filter_by_date(), whose details also apply here: the services that run on at least one day of the period are kept (or dropped).

With trim = TRUE, the kept services are then cut to the period: the start_date and end_date of their calendar entries are clipped to it (entries left without any day are removed), and the calendar_dates entries outside it are removed. Each service then runs on exactly the same days within the period as before, and on no day outside it. The feed_info table is not changed. With trim = FALSE, the services are kept as a whole, so they may still run on days outside the period.

The period is first clipped to the dates covered by the calendar and calendar_dates tables, on which the services can run, so the days of the period outside them add no work. The memory used still grows with the number of days the period shares with each service's calendar.

See also

filter_by_date(), get_active_services(), get_dates()

Other filtering functions: filter_by_agency_id(), filter_by_date(), filter_by_route_id(), filter_by_route_type(), filter_by_service_id(), filter_by_shape_id(), filter_by_spatial_extent(), filter_by_stop_id(), filter_by_time_of_day(), filter_by_trip_id(), filter_by_weekday()

Examples

data_path <- system.file("extdata/ggl_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")
gtfs <- read_gtfs(data_path)

gtfs$calendar
#>    service_id monday tuesday wednesday thursday friday saturday sunday
#>        <char>  <int>   <int>     <int>    <int>  <int>    <int>  <int>
#> 1:         WE      0       0         0        0      0        1      1
#> 2:         WD      1       1         1        1      1        0      0
#>    start_date   end_date
#>        <Date>     <Date>
#> 1: 2006-07-01 2006-07-31
#> 2: 2006-07-01 2006-07-31
gtfs$calendar_dates
#>    service_id       date exception_type
#>        <char>     <Date>          <int>
#> 1:         WD 2006-07-03              2
#> 2:         WE 2006-07-03              1
#> 3:         WD 2006-07-04              2
#> 4:         WE 2006-07-04              1

# keeps the services that run in the first week of july 2006, with their
# calendars cut to that week
smaller_gtfs <- filter_by_period(gtfs, "2006-07-01", "2006-07-07")
smaller_gtfs$calendar
#>    service_id monday tuesday wednesday thursday friday saturday sunday
#>        <char>  <int>   <int>     <int>    <int>  <int>    <int>  <int>
#> 1:         WE      0       0         0        0      0        1      1
#> 2:         WD      1       1         1        1      1        0      0
#>    start_date   end_date
#>        <Date>     <Date>
#> 1: 2006-07-01 2006-07-07
#> 2: 2006-07-01 2006-07-07

# keeps the same services, with their whole calendars
smaller_gtfs <- filter_by_period(
  gtfs,
  "2006-07-01",
  "2006-07-07",
  trim = FALSE
)
smaller_gtfs$calendar
#>    service_id monday tuesday wednesday thursday friday saturday sunday
#>        <char>  <int>   <int>     <int>    <int>  <int>    <int>  <int>
#> 1:         WE      0       0         0        0      0        1      1
#> 2:         WD      1       1         1        1      1        0      0
#>    start_date   end_date
#>        <Date>     <Date>
#> 1: 2006-07-01 2006-07-31
#> 2: 2006-07-01 2006-07-31

# dates may also be given as Date objects. drops the services that run in
# the period
smaller_gtfs <- filter_by_period(
  gtfs,
  as.Date("2006-07-03"),
  as.Date("2006-07-04"),
  keep = FALSE
)
smaller_gtfs$calendar
#>    service_id monday tuesday wednesday thursday friday saturday sunday
#>        <char>  <int>   <int>     <int>    <int>  <int>    <int>  <int>
#> 1:         WD      1       1         1        1      1        0      0
#>    start_date   end_date
#>        <Date>     <Date>
#> 1: 2006-07-01 2006-07-31
